name: Suprematism. This is a supplemental design reference and is not claimed as a directly named style in the source collection.
visualIdentity: A few abstract squares, circles, crosses, and bars sit on an open field. Relative size, angle, balance, and negative space carry the composition. Forms use black, white, and restrained primary colors, with flat fills and no illustrative textures.
suitableUses: Explicitly listed good fits are UI and product storytelling, editorial and minimalist layouts, and motion posters or staged geometric compositions. Inferred suitability includes sparse artistic statements and exhibition openers with few words.
limitations: Adapt or omit the style when recomposition changes hierarchy without explaining the subject, when an anchored subject crops important details, or when pinning disrupts the layout. Dense text and paragraphs are unsuitable. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production or validated physics.
palette: The palette is an unsupplied suggestion, used only when no task, brand, or reference colors exist: background #FFFFFF, foreground #000000, accent_1 #C92B2B, accent_2 #E8BE30, accent_3 #2453A0. Gradients are disabled, colors stay discrete, and supplied exact colors override these. Foreground on background measures 21:1, accent_1 on background 5.435:1, accent_2 with foreground 11.839:1, and accent_3 on background 7.447:1. These are two-color checks only, so composited frames must be rechecked.
motionAndInteraction: Forms shift slowly in position, rotation, and proportion while remaining abstract. Movement should be smooth and coherent, with deliberate cuts preserved and no automatic bounce, springs, or extra in-between poses. Motion patterns motion-007, motion-012, and motion-015 are optional candidates only. Interactive delivery may map scroll progress and should offer a static reduced-motion state, while video must not depend on scroll.
audio: Audio is unspecified for this style, and the source imposes no fixed music, voice, or effect requirement. Based on topic and audience, options include background music, voiceover, sound effects, ambience, or silence, chosen so they do not compete with narration. Requested audio and supplied assets take priority. Speech intelligibility, balance, and absence of clipping must be verified.
assetRequirements: No specific fonts, images, or audio files are listed. Any text must be real, readable text, and video fonts and assets must be loaded before rendering. Topic-specific assets may replace the example objects in motion patterns. Duration, aspect ratio, resolution, frame rate, and output directory are template placeholders and remain unspecified.
combinations: Suprematism is usually strongest alone. The single suggested hybrid is style-093 kinetic typography, where up to five words act as weighted bars in black or one primary color with slow drift, rotation, and no bounce or textures. Avoid paragraphs, dense typography, and fast kinetic sequences. Motion patterns are optional additions.
productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default pipeline for composition timing, validation, and export, using a paused GSAP timeline registered in window.__timelines. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a requirement, and that reason must be recorded. Flat SVG is the recommended renderer, GSAP is the primary motion engine, and Motion is optional. chroma.js is optional for color checks, and Canvas 2D is an alternative.
